etymologies.etymologyHTML: From chuck +‎ -le.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, archaic) To make the sound of a chicken; to cluck.
(transitive, archaic) To call together, or call to follow, as a hen calls her chickens; to cluck.

quote.citation: 1690, [John] Dryden, Don Sebastian, King of Portugal: […], London:  […]  Jo. Hindmarsh, […], →OCLC, (please specify the page number):
quote.text: if these Birds are within distance, here's that will chuckle 'em together

definitions.definition: (transitive, archaic) To fondle; to indulge or pamper.
